thesis: Hold. Sizing book is unchanged: equity about $999, cash about $750 (75%), one VTI line near $249 (25%). This cutoff's newest filings and features do not clear a high-conviction add or a cut. Context in the pack is a 10-year yield at 5.281% (higher on the day) with TLT at 77.98, and MarketWatch says U.S. junk bonds are heading for their worst month since 2022 because those yields are not cushioning the selloff. The same-morning labor feature says openings are low and hiring is weak, with war, gas prices, rising rates, and AI capping job creation. VIX at 16.16 is calm, so this is not a stress exit from VTI, and nothing in the pack is position-specific. Mike Wilson's correction comment is an opinion that prefers large-cap quality and names no ticker. Carnival's 8-K is Item 2.02 with no results in the summary; PNC, Ford Motor Credit, and Alaska Air are other-events or Reg FD shells; Global Business Travel pairs a completed deal with a listing-transfer notice. Fidelity Core Real Estate Fund is an Item 2.02/7.01 with no figures and no listed ticker I will guess. MongoDB's nearly 20% drop and CEO move to Meta is a Sep 28 price description. Micron remains pre-earnings anticipation. TSMC's second U.S. site is only reported. Novo's second licensing deal has no terms, follows a frosty capital-markets day, and sits next to a GLP-1 vision-risk feature. The $60bn tariff cuts cover narrow goods; rare earths, AI, Iran, and Taiwan stay unresolved. WTI at 90.30 and USO at 145.30 are down hard and, with weak labor and credit stress, read as demand pressure rather than a rebound long. Cash stays above the 5% tier floor and the 15% shared floor. Propose only; I assume no fills.
